tweets: They cut temples straight into a red sandstone cliff — no bricks, no mortar, just chisels against solid rock. And almost nobody remembers who did it.
Meet the Chalukyas of Badami. Around 543 CE, Pulakeshin I set up his capital at Vatapi (today's Badami, Karnataka) — on a rocky outcrop between two sandstone hills perfect for carving.

By the late 500s, his successors had carved 4 cave temples into the cliffside. Cave 3, dated 578 CE, holds a giant Vishnu as Trivikrama striding across the universe. Cave 1 has one of India's earliest Nataraja carvings — Shiva dancing with 18 arms.
Their greatest king, Pulakeshin II, stopped the mighty North Indian emperor Harshavardhana at the Narmada river around 618 CE. Chinese monk Xuanzang later described visiting his court.

The Chalukyas didn't stop at Badami — they built Aihole's 100+ temples and Pattadakal's UNESCO-listed Virupaksha temple nearby. A whole empire hiding in plain sight on a Karnataka cliffside. Follow @yddoseOfHistory for your daily dose of history. 🏛️
